title: Joao Almeida to miss Giro d’Italia after sickness affects preparation
content:
Joao Almeida has announced that he will not race the Giro d’Italia, the primary goal of his season, after sickness damaged his preparation.

“I just won’t quite be ready in time,” the UAE Team Emirates rider wrote on Instagram.

Almeida, who finished third and won the young rider category in the 2023 Giro, was one of the top two favourites for next month’s race, having also finished on the podium of last year’s Vuelta a Espana.

The 27-year-old’s withdrawal further entrenches Jonas Vingegaard’s status as the overwhelming favourite — bidding to become the only active rider to have won all three Grand Tours — having only taken victory at the Vuelta by one minute and 16 seconds over the Portuguese rider.

Now, Vingegaard’s primary opposition is likely to come in the shape of Red Bull-BORA-Hansgrohe’s young Italian hopeful Giulio Pellizzari, who impressed in taking victory at the Tour of the Alps last week.

Other contenders include EF Education-EasyPost’s Richard Carapaz, who finished third at the Giro last year, and INEOS Grenadiers pair Egan Bernal and Thymen Arensman, though it would be a major shock if any of this trio won the pink jersey.

“Unfortunately I won’t be at the start of the Giro d’Italia next month as planned,” Almeida wrote on social media on Monday morning. “Sickness in the past months has affected my preparations too much and has meant I just won’t quite be ready in time which is a shame as it’s a race I love so much.

“After talking it through with the team we decided it was best to take a rest period and switch focus to new goals later in the season. We haven’t set out those new goals yet but that will be done calmly in the next few weeks.

“For now it’s time to first rest-up a bit and build things back up slowly. Best of luck to the guys for the Giro, (I) will be cheering from home.”

Almeida’s decision also has wider implications for UAE’s season. Pogacar racing the Giro is not an option, given his Classics exploits and Tour de France preparations, while Isaac del Toro, second at the race last year, had been slated to be the Slovenian’s key domestique in July.

Given the fact that Del Toro missed last week’s Ardennes races to focus on recovery from a torn thigh muscle, his condition does not appear good enough to effectively swap roles with Almeida.

Instead, it appears most likely that UAE’s riders will be free to pursue stage victories — with the likes of Adam Yates (himself a former Tour podium finisher), Jhonatan Narvaez, Jay Vine, Marc Soler, and Jan Christen all potential winners on hilly and mountainous terrain.

The Giro starts in Bulgaria on Friday May 8. It will then travel from south to north through Italy, with a mountainous final week in the Alps and Dolomites, before finishing in Rome on May 31.
